answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the tundra checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The river graph is rebuilt each epoch, as a result the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the harbor audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 6 times its size, so a group of 4 keys loses far more than 4 single identities would. That is 34 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
